segments: The Chronography of Barhebraeus.
Then Batu said:
"Except for Möngke, I see no man who is capable of properly managing a great kingdom such as this."
And all of them said:
"It is fitting and right."
And when that wise Möngke showed some hesitation,
they took him by force,
and made him sit upon the throne.
And Batu, together with all the royal princes, bowed down on their knees and did homage to him.
And Batu took the cup according to custom and gave him to drink.
And when the kingdom was confirmed to him, in the year six hundred and forty-nine of the Arabs [649 AH],
on the ninth of the fourth month,
she, the faithful queen, all-wise, Sorghaghtani Beki, the mother of Möngke, began to win over all the chiefs and nobles with abundant gifts and presents,
and to subdue the rebels with good promises.
And while they were awaiting the arrival of the sons of Güyük Khan and of their mother Oghul Qaimish,
there came a certain man from those who train lions as it were for the amusement of the princes, and said:
"When I had lost a lion,
I went three days' journey searching for it.
And I came to the tents of the sons of Güyük Khan, who are coming here.
And I saw a wagon that was broken,
and a youth sitting beside it and repairing it.
And he called to me to help him.
And when I approached,
I saw that that wagon was completely full of armor and weapons of war.
And I asked that youth:
'What are these?' And he said to me with astonishment:
'How, when you are one of us,
do you not know these things? All these wagons that are with us are like this.'
And when I left him, I came and made it known to you;
now therefore you know [what to do]."
Then Möngke Khan sent a chief whose name was Mengeser with two thousand horsemen to meet the sons of Güyük Khan,
and he said to them:
"First you with a few men ought to come to Möngke Khan and see him,
and afterwards your forces may come."
And when they were unable to answer with harsh words,
they did so.
And when they came,
after three days during which they ate, drank, and rested,
Möngke {OCR: ܫܘܼܢܓܵܐ for ܡܘܼܢܓܵܐ} Khan disclosed the matter to them.
And they were ashamed,
and were utterly unable to utter a word.
